data: Confirmed water ice in Martian soil
Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.
Phoenix is a planetary lander built by Lockheed Martin in USA. Confirmed water ice in Martian soil. Mission ended in 2008.
First confirmation of water ice in the Martian arctic regolith; first soft propulsive Mars landing since Viking 2
Lost during landing in 1999; the failure led NASA to review its “faster, better, cheaper” approach
First successful Mars lander; biology experiments
Second US Mars surface lander (Utopia Planitia 1976-09-03). Twin of Viking 1 lander; ran biology, soil chemistry + meteorology until 1980

First spacecraft to physically touch Martian water ice. Phoenix's robotic arm scooped ice that sublimated in front of its cameras within hours — direct visual confirmation of the subsurface ice that Mars Odyssey's neutron spectrometer had inferred from orbit. Operated 157 sols before the northern winter froze its solar panels.
